Forecast Discussion

Friday night’s front is off the coast, and cooler air pours over the mountains today on a gusty northwest wind. Skies clear quickly, but the wind keeps it feeling colder than the thermometer reads.

High pressure settles over the Tennessee Valley Sunday, and the wind eases. A dry disturbance crosses late Sunday night and kicks the wind back up early Monday. Valleys turn chilly at night under clear skies and dry air.

The high moves off the Carolina coast Tuesday with a pleasant afternoon. A weak front drops in from the north late Tuesday night. It is moisture-starved and only takes a few degrees off Wednesday.

A stronger front crosses the mountains Thursday. Showers develop Thursday morning, especially on the west side of the Appalachians, and change to snow showers late Thursday night as cold air arrives behind the front.

Friday brings our first snow showers of the season especially near the Tennessee line and at higher elevations, with flurries reaching the Blue Ridge (the eastern escarpment). It is cold and windy. The Snowman-O-Mometer will have to leave hibernation Monday, probably- our 5-day outlook for snow.
